name: Grand Summoner Govannon

facts.text: Grand Summoner Govannon is the level-80 final of Summoner's Hall for all three realms' raids; the Offline DAoC build gives him 200,000 health (300,000 originally).

At 80% he grows stronger and calls a summoned sacrifice and a summoned demon. The sacrifice walks to his feet and is consumed there; once it has been consumed and the demon is dead, the Shade of Aelfgar rises and joins the fight, stunning with Aelfgar's Shout.
At 50% he drops his elven shape, becomes a demon, heals to full health and hits harder still.
He casts Govannon's Shroud of Agony (an area damage over time) and a bleeding Demon's Scar, sends a random attacker to a fixed spot, and cannot be hurt when drawn past his tether.
Allakhazam lists him as a level-80 demon. A period player wrote that you first see an elf caster, then a taller shape, and at 60% his true demon form; 43 people took close to 30 minutes.
Bot chat says he starts as an elf and finishes as a demon, and tells a 'shield node' story that the script does not have (hearsay).
Gofannon (Govannon) is the smith son of Don in the Welsh tales (to verify the spelling and role in the Mabinogion).
Aelfgar is an Old English name; aelf means elf and gar spear (to verify).

story:
Govannon is the name of a smith in the old tales of the west, a maker who forged for the gods. The Grand Summoner took the name because he too is a maker, and what he makes is bargains. He sits in the deepest room of the hall that lies under all three frontiers, in a chamber built to the pattern of Legion's own, and he calls. The dead of Albion, Midgard and Hibernia hear him through the floors of their frontier dungeons, and some of them answer.

He wears the shape of one of the sidhe, a tall caster in fine robes, and for a while he fights like one. When he has been hurt enough to take you seriously he makes a bargain in front of you: a sacrifice walks to his feet across the floor, and a demon stands up beside him. Let the sacrifice reach him and the price is paid, and when the demon falls, the Shade of Aelfgar comes to collect, an old spear-ghost whose shout drops men where they stand. At half his strength he stops pretending. The elf splits and the demon steps out of it, whole again, as if the first half of the fight had happened to someone else. Nobody knows which one was the real Govannon. Possibly he does not know either.
legend: Govannon is two fights. At 80% kill the sacrifice before it reaches his feet, or the Shade of Aelfgar comes once the demon dies; stun break for the shade's shout. At 50% he turns demon and heals to full, so pace your power: the second half is the real fight. Don't drag him off his spot, he can't be hurt past his tether. Period raids took about 40 people and half an hour. The shield node story is old raid talk; nobody has found the node.

aggro: You came down through your own floors to me. I have been calling your dead for years. Now I call you.

phases.text: A bargain, then. Walk to me, little sacrifice. Rise, my demon.
The price is paid. Aelfgar, come and collect.
Enough of this skin. Look at me as I am.

slay: You will answer when I call, now.

lairEntry: The deepest room. It is built like Legion's own.
A tall figure in robes is calling. The dead listen.

phases.text: A sacrifice walks toward Govannon. Stop it!
The Shade of Aelfgar rises to collect the price!
Govannon tears off his elven shape. A demon stands!

atmosphere.realmFirstKill: The Grand Summoner is silent. The calling has stopped.

loremasterTopic.text: The Grand Summoner, named for a smith of the old tales because he too is a maker; what he makes is bargains. He wears a sidhe's shape until half his strength is gone, and then the demon steps out of it, whole. Stop his sacrifice reaching his feet, or the Shade of Aelfgar comes to collect.

bookPage: Of the bargains of the Grand Summoner, from a sidhe magicker who had been his student, as near as I could follow her. Every calling has a price, she said, and he always pays it, because a maker who does not pay is only a thief. The price walks to him on its own feet. If it arrives, the debt is settled, and the one he owes, an old ghost named Aelfgar, comes up out of the floor to take what is owed. If it does not arrive, he must find another way to pay, and he does not like that. She said the elf you see is the shape he was paid in, long ago. She would not say what paid it.
